judged_text: The rewritten Google Meet fallback crashes with a TypeError when destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, because mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and the code calls .integration on it without a guard. Any booking with location = Google Meet and no destination calendar (eventType.destinationCalendar and organizerUser.destinationCalendar both absent, or payment/confirm flows passing `destinationCalendar: []`) throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` instead of falling back to Cal Video — the exact scenario the original `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` check existed for, per its own comment 'Fallback to Cal Video if Google Meet is selected w/o a Google Cal'. The null-safe behavior was silently destroyed in this iteration.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the new fallback logic does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then immediately reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without null/undefined guarding: `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")`. When `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, `undefined`, or an empty array (which this diff now produces in multiple places, e.g. `destinationCalendar: []` in payment/confirm flows and `null` in `handleNewBooking`), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` becomes `undefined`, causing `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` instead of safely falling back as the prior optional-chaining check did.
